instruction: Compare iPhone 15 with iPhone 14 and iPhone 13

metadata.explanation: This variation compares the standard iPhone models (not Pro Max) across three generations (15, 14, 13). While still focusing on iPhones like the original task, this variation targets the standard line instead of Pro Max models, providing meaningful diversity while maintaining the same task complexity and interaction pattern. The evaluator reuses existing functions to parse and verify the comparison URL.
metadata.verification_notes: Reuses existing getter (get_active_tab_url_parse) and metric (check_direct_json_object) functions. No custom functions needed. The expected model identifiers follow Apple's URL naming convention for standard iPhone models.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic is semantically correct: get_active_tab_url_parse properly extracts and parses URL query parameters, splits comma-separated values into a list as needed
Metric logic is correct: check_direct_json_object properly compares JSON objects with ignore_list_order support, ensuring all three iPhone models are present regardless of order
Coverage is complete: evaluator verifies all three iPhone models (15, 14, 13) are present in the modelList parameter

URL structure assumption: evaluator assumes Apple's comparison uses a 'modelList' query parameter with specific model identifiers (iphone-15, iphone-14, iphone-13), which may not match actual Apple URL conventions
Indirect verification: only checks URL structure, not whether the comparison page actually loaded or displays the three models being compared
Active tab dependency: relies on accessibility tree correctly identifying the active tab URL, which may fail if the user is on a different tab or the URL changed
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding a fallback getter to verify page content (e.g., parse the HTML to confirm the three iPhone models are displayed on the comparison page)
Document the exact URL pattern expected from Apple's comparison tool to help with debugging if the evaluation fails
Consider using a more robust verification that checks both URL parameters AND page content to ensure the comparison was actually completed
